answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn from tasks. A newcomer’s velvet profile carries little weight until it completes independently verified work; payouts then grow with a history of reliable delivery. If one operator splits into many identities, each must fund its own stake and build its own record, while correlated behavior can trigger audits and slash deposits. The signal is costly capital at risk, and a failed swarm sends a ripple of losses across the attacker’s identities.
